data: Baja California (the state containing Mexicali) is highlighted as one of the most concerning water-stress cases in Mexico, with a 2025 regional dryness index of 4.67 out of 5 — near the highest recorded level — while 71% of Mexican territory faces high or very high water stress.
source_title: Water Stress: Strategic Risk for Business in Mexico
excerpt: According to the State Citizen Water Commission, 2025 was one of the driest years for the region since 1950, reaching an index of 4.67 out of 5, placing it near its highest recorded level.

data: The Mexicali region is characterized academically as an area threatened by water scarcity and overexploitation of its water sources, which underlies the socio-environmental conflict over industrial water use there.
source_title: Elements of Socio-Environmental Conflict: The Constellation Brands Brewery and Mexicali Water
excerpt: This study aims to determine the extent to which such notions are incorporated into a region threatened by scarcity and overexploitation of water sources.

data: Reports on the Constellation Brands brewery dispute describe the Mexicali Valley as a desert region with an over-exploited aquifer fed by the Colorado River, amid serious water shortages in the broader Baja California region.
source_title: Mexicali Resiste Activist VS. Constellation Brands: Activists continue to demand WATER RIGHTS and FREEDOM
excerpt: This desert region has an over-exploited aquifer that is fed by the Colorado River with serious water shortages and serious drought issues in Tijuana, Tecate, Rosarito and Ensenada.

data: In 2017, mass protests erupted in Mexicali over a planned Constellation Brands brewery, with more than 12,000 residents taking to the streets; some protesters were later charged with 'dispossession of state buildings' and 'deprivation of liberty of the police,' though investigators later cleared them.
source_title: Mexicali Resiste VS. Constellation Brands: Activists Demand WATER RIGHTS and FREEDOM
excerpt: Local outrage peaked in 2017, when over 12,000 residents of Mexicali took to the streets, including the members of Mexicali Resiste who now stand trial.

data: Since January 2017, the activist group Mexicali Resiste organized ongoing marches and boycott campaigns opposing the brewery's plan to consume 20 million cubic meters of water annually from the Valley of Mexicali, including a January 2020 march at the Vicente Guerrero Monument.
source_title: "Mexicali Resiste" Fights For Water Rights Against Constellation Brands Compromising Quality Of Life In Baja, California
excerpt: Since January 2017, Mexicali Resiste has maintained a strong opposition to the Constellation Brands factory that would consume 20 million cubic meters of water annually from the Valley of Mexicali.

data: In February 2020, Mexico's National Human Rights Commission released a report determining that the approval and installation process for the Constellation Brands brewery violated the human right to water, to the detriment of the population and farmers of the Valley of Mexicali.
source_title: Mexicali Resiste Activist vs. Constellation Brands: Activists Demand Water Rights and Freedom - Wine Industry Advisor
excerpt: Then, in February 2020 the National Human Rights Commission released a report that determined that the process of the approval and installation of the Constellation Brands Brewery violates the human right to water, which would lead to the detriment of the population and farmers of the Valley of Mexicali.

data: Social protests against the brewery project began as early as April 2015, driven partly by lack of transparency from state government promoters regarding the construction of a dedicated aqueduct for the plant's sole use.
source_title: Elements of Socio-Environmental Conflict: The Constellation Brands Brewery and Mexicali Water
excerpt: Since the announcement of the intention to build the brewery in Mexicali in April 2015, a series of social protests were unleashed in the municipality against the project itself and the lack of transparency implemented by the state governments' promoters when explaining the use of public resources to construct an aqueduct for the brewery's sole use.

data: Under Mexico's National Water Law (LAN), industrial water use is allocated through CONAGUA-issued concession titles permitting extraction from rivers, lakes and groundwater; concessions are denied if the site lies in an overexploited aquifer, and high-water-use sectors like beverages and metallurgy face rigorous audits for recycling/reuse compliance.
source_title: The facts on industrial water usage in Mexico
excerpt: Under the LAN, water for use in the industrial sector is allocated through concession titles that allow extraction from rivers, lakes, and groundwater.

data: On Dec. 5, 2025, Mexico's Senate approved a new General Water Law and amendments to the National Water Law, reinforcing water as a human right that takes priority over industrial uses, banning transfers of water concessions between private parties, and creating new water-crime offenses with fines up to roughly MX$5,657,000.
source_title: Mexico Approves New General Water Law and Amends National Water Law | Insights | Holland & Knight
excerpt: The Mexican Senate on Dec. 5, 2025, approved the General Water Law (Ley General de Aguas) and amendments to the National Water Law (Ley de Aguas Nacionales), marking a significant shift in the regulatory framework governing water resources in Mexico.

data: Under the reformed law, any concession or authorization for water use must prioritize human and domestic consumption over industrial uses, and CONAGUA is empowered to reduce or cancel industrial water concessions without limitation during scarcity, emergency, or hydrological imbalance situations.
source_title: Nueva Ley General de Aguas y Reforma a la Ley de Aguas Nacionales
excerpt: Any concession, extension, authorization or allocation of water must prioritize human and domestic consumption over industrial uses. In situations of scarcity, emergency or hydrological imbalance, CONAGUA is empowered to reduce or cancel water concessions granted to industries without limitation of amount.

data: The amended LAN eliminates concession holders' right to freely transfer water concession rights to third parties and requires CONAGUA to resolve reassignment requests within 20 business days, expanding CONAGUA's regulatory authority, grounds for non-compliance, and applicable sanctions for industrial concessionaires.
source_title: Amendments to Mexico's National Waters Law: Key considerations for industrial water concessionaires
excerpt: The right of concessionaires to freely transfer their concession rights to third parties is eliminated from the LAN.

data: Mexico is one of only four countries (with India, Egypt and Turkey) expected to account for over half of the global GDP exposed to high water stress by 2050, reflecting the country's severe baseline water stress.
source_title: 25 Countries, Housing One-Quarter of the Population, Face Extremely High Water Stress
excerpt: Just four countries — India, Mexico, Egypt and Turkey — account for over half of the exposed GDP in 2050.

data: Under WRI Aqueduct projections for Mexican states, Nuevo León (where Monterrey is located) is projected to reach a medium-high level of water depletion by 2030, in the 20%-40% range, while many neighboring/other industrial states face extremely high depletion.
source_title: 14 Mexican states could face extreme water stress by 2030
excerpt: six states — Jalisco, México state, Michoacán, Puebla, Tamaulipas and Tlaxcala — are expected to experience high water depletion, ranging between 40% and 80%, while Nuevo León could reach a medium-high level of depletion, between 20% and 40%.

data: WRI Aqueduct's Baseline Water Stress (BWS) methodology classifies any location with a score above 80% as 'extremely high' stress, meaning severe competition for water resources among agricultural, industrial and domestic users — a threshold framework directly applicable to assessing sites in northern Mexico's stressed basins.
source_title: Prioritize Basins: Target Water Challenges by Thresholds | World Resources Institute
excerpt: An Extremely High >80% BWS (Baseline Water Stress) Score indicates significant water stress in the specific location.

data: Monterrey experienced its worst modern water crisis in 2022, when the Cerro Prieto dam that supplies the metro area dropped below 1% capacity by July, causing millions of residents to lose tap water access and sparking protests.
source_title: Water Crisis in Monterrey: A Student's Journey - Mexico News Daily
excerpt: A perfect storm of drought, demand and aging infrastructure caused dams to dry up — Cerro Prieto, which long supplied the Monterrey metro area with water, dropped below 1% capacity by July.

data: Protests escalated in mid-July 2022 when residents demonstrated against pipelines used by Monterrey's water utility (SADM) to divert water to the city, and pipes were deliberately set on fire to halt the diversion plan.
source_title: Drought in northern Mexico brings water shortages and social unrest
excerpt: Protests escalated in mid-July, when residents demonstrated against the use of pipelines by SADM, the water utility company of Monterrey, to divert as much as 500 litres of water per second towards the city.

data: The 2022 crisis sparked widespread civil unrest, including residents blocking major highways and setting fire to pipes intended to divert emergency water flows, with anger also directed at large factories that continued operating using private wells under federal concessions while residents went without water.
source_title: Taps have run dry in Monterrey, Mexico, where there is water for factories but not for residents
excerpt: The crisis has sparked widespread upheaval, with frustrated residents blocking major highways in protest and people in other parts of the state setting fire to pipes that were supposed to divert emergency flows to the city.

data: Street protests broke out in Monterrey in June 2022 as residents grew angry over prolonged water rationing that began in March 2022 amid a severe drought.
source_title: Dry town: Mexican city of 5 million without water for weeks - CSMonitor.com
excerpt: anger is growing among residents and street protests have broken out in Monterrey.

data: Historical precedent exists for water-related unrest in Monterrey: forced water rationing in the past spawned protests that escalated into mass rallies, blockades, seizure of water service trucks, and occupation of government buildings.
source_title: Urban water management in Monterrey
excerpt: Forced water rationing spawned water protests that escalated to larger organized mass rallies, blockades, seizure of water service trucks, taking over of government buildings, and the holding hostage of water delivery drivers.

data: In late 2025 Mexico approved a new General Water Law (Ley General de Aguas) and amendments to the National Water Law (Ley de Aguas Nacionales), which prioritize the human right to water over other uses including industrial use, and restrict changes to water concession use types (e.g. agricultural to industrial).
source_title: México aprueba la nueva Ley General de Aguas y reformas
excerpt: Human Right to Water: The law reinforces water as a fundamental human right, prioritizing personal and domestic consumption over other uses.

data: The reform eliminates concessionaires' ability to freely transfer water concession rights to third parties, centralizing all reassignment authority exclusively with CONAGUA, which must prioritize reallocation toward the human right to water, food security, and national development.
source_title: Nueva Ley General de Aguas y Reforma a la Ley de Aguas Nacionales
excerpt: The right of concessionaires to freely transfer their concession rights to third parties is eliminated from the LAN.

data: In situations of scarcity, emergency, or hydrological imbalance, CONAGUA is empowered to reduce or cancel water concessions granted to industries without limitation of amount — directly relevant to industrial plants operating during drought emergencies like those declared in Nuevo León.
source_title: Amendments to Mexico's National Waters Law: Key considerations for industrial water concessionaires
excerpt: A new concept known as "reassignment" is introduced, pursuant to which the Mexican National Water Commission ("CONAGUA") may dispose of volumes of water available in the national water reserve fund and assign or grant them under concession, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the LAN and its regulations.

data: During the 2022 drought emergency, Mexico's national water authority CONAGUA issued measures allowing holders of agricultural or industrial water concessions to be ordered to permit their use by third parties, directly affecting industrial water users in Monterrey.
source_title: Mexico declares drought emergency
excerpt: Among the measures, holders of water concessions for agricultural or industrial use can be ordered to allow their use by third parties.

data: Mexico's foundational water law, the Ley de Aguas Nacionales (1992), regulates the exploitation, use, and enjoyment of national waters, their distribution and control, and mandates preservation of water quantity and quality for sustainable development, forming the base regulatory framework industrial users like plants in Monterrey must comply with.
source_title: comisión nacional del agua Ley de Aguas Nacionales y su Reglamento
excerpt: tiene por objeto regular la explotación, uso o aprovechamiento de dichas aguas, su distribución y control, así como la preservación de su cantidad y calidad para lograr su desarrollo integral sustentable.

data: Arizona (where Chandler is located) falls into the 'high water stress' category on WRI's Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas, one tier below the most severe 'extremely high' category.
source_title: Mapping the strain on our water supply - The Washington Post
excerpt: Neighboring Arizona was among four states in the somewhat-less-perilous "high stress" category.

data: The Colorado River, a key water source for Chandler, has experienced federally declared shortages since 2022, with more frequent shortages expected, though the city has significant groundwater storage as a buffer.
source_title: Chandler Drought Preparedness | City of Chandler, AZ
excerpt: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation declared the first-ever shortage on the Colorado River in 2022.

data: Chandler has substantial groundwater reserves to fall back on, but relies on multiple surface water sources including the Colorado, Salt and Verde rivers, whose average flows have been declining.
source_title: Chandler Drought Preparedness | City of Chandler, AZ
excerpt: Chandler has enough water stored underground to last for roughly 20 to 30 years.

data: Chandler is preparing for potential cuts of 20-40% to its Colorado River water supply starting in 2027, reflecting ongoing regional conflict among Colorado River Basin states over water allocation.
source_title: Chandler begins girding for cuts in water supply | News | chandlernews.com
excerpt: Chandler is preparing for cuts between 20% and 40%.

data: A proposed data center project in Chandler sparked public and expert opposition over its water use amid an approaching Arizona water crisis, with residents and researchers questioning the tradeoff of water use for low employment.
source_title: How much water will Chandler's data center project use?
excerpt: That's a lot of water spent on a low-employment data center at a time when Arizona cities face up to 20% cuts in water from the Colorado River

data: Local officials describe the Colorado River situation as reaching crisis proportions in 2026, with a public panel in Chandler discussing looming water supply cuts.
source_title: Water crisis looming in 2026, experts say | News | queencreektribune.com
excerpt: A dry winter has further depleted the Colorado River, a main source of water for Chandler.

data: Chandler falls under the Phoenix Active Management Area (AMA), created by Arizona's 1980 Groundwater Management Act, which imposes the state's highest level of groundwater regulation including metering, reporting, and conservation requirements on industrial users.
source_title: AZ's Groundwater Management Act of 1980 | Arizona Department of Water Resources
excerpt: At the same time, the law required that its active-management areas, or AMAs, wean themselves fromgroundwater pumping.

data: Within AMAs like Phoenix (which covers Chandler), municipal, industrial and agricultural water users have been subject to progressively rigorous water management plan requirements since 1987, with the goal of achieving 'safe yield' between groundwater withdrawal and recharge.
source_title: Arizona Water | GPEC - Greater Phoenix Economic Council
excerpt: Municipal water providers, industrial users, and agricultural water users have been subject to these requirements since the First Management Plan became effective in 1987.

data: Under the AMA framework, ADWR develops a new management plan for each AMA every ten years, imposing increasingly rigorous conservation and efficiency requirements across sectors, including industrial users.
source_title: arizona water
excerpt: Every ten years, ADWR develops a new management plan for each AMA, with increasingly rigorous conservation and efficiency requirements for all sectors.

data: Chandler has its own local drought management plan, updated to include tiered stages triggered by surface water shortage conditions, which governs how the city responds to Colorado River shortfalls affecting industrial and other users.
source_title: Chandler begins girding for cuts in water supply | News | chandlernews.com
excerpt: The City of Chandler updated its drought management plan on Nov. 13, partly because officials know they may need it very soon.
